title: Orsen and the Echo
premise: Tamsin Ishikawa, a xenolinguist whose dreams have gone silent in every human tongue, is ferrying cargo on the long route when the Meridian returns from deep space with its crew aged backward into children who speak a language that predates their own lives. The two fleets guarding the truce each claim the ship, and Tamsin discovers the 'echo' language the children carry is proof the truce was built on a fabricated first contact. To keep the lie alive long enough to broker peace, she must teach the children to forget what they know, while falling for the Meridian's de-aged captain, who remembers loving her from a future she never lived. In the end she chooses truth over the truce, broadcasting the echo language to both fleets and forcing them to build a real peace instead of a borrowed one.
about_author: Cyrus Ravensworth is the pen name of a former shipping-route radio operator who spent eleven years listening to languages he couldn't understand cross the dark between stations. He writes about people who translate for a living and pay for it in sleep.

chapters.title: The Silent Route
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She runs cargo between colonies that have stopped trading words, dreaming only in an alien cadence she can't name. Establishes her isolation, her fading human languages, and the fragile fleet truce that keeps her route alive. Emotional beat: loneliness mistaken for competence.

chapters.title: Meridian, Returning
chapters.summary: Tamsin intercepts a distress call and finds the deep-space ship Meridian drifting home, its crew of forty now children under ten, speaking fluently in a language no human has recorded. Her translator implant fails; her dreams don't. Emotional beat: awe curdling into dread as she realizes she understands them.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Wreck
chapters.summary: Both truce fleets converge to claim the Meridian. Captain Sefa Okafor, de-aged but retaining fragmented memories of a future including Tamsin, shields the children with instinctive authority. Tamsin is conscripted by both sides as neutral linguist. Emotional beat: being needed by enemies simultaneously.

chapters.title: What the Children Know
chapters.summary: Tamsin decodes the echo language and finds it contains detailed accounts of a first contact that officially never happened — the event the truce was supposedly founded on. The records are decades old, older than the children. Emotional beat: the vertigo of holding a truth that could kill thousands.

chapters.title: The Lie That Holds
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV interwoven with fleet council scenes. She learns admirals on both sides already suspect the fabrication; the truce survives only because neither will admit it first. She begins teaching the children silence. Emotional beat: complicity — protecting peace by burying justice.

chapters.title: A Future She Never Lived
chapters.summary: Sefa confesses his fragmentary memories: in the erased timeline, he and Tamsin were partners, and she died exposing the same lie. Loving him feels like grieving someone else's life. Duty demands she report his knowledge; loyalty makes her keep it. Emotional beat: love as evidence of a crime.

chapters.title: Truce Expiry
chapters.summary: The truce clock runs down. A fleet hardliner seizes three of the children as 'evidence,' and skirmishes flare along the route. Tamsin's transmissions are monitored; her careful silences start reading as treason to both sides. Emotional beat: the walls of neutrality closing in.

chapters.title: The Echo Speaks
chapters.summary: Under interrogation-adjacent pressure, the eldest child breaks the taught silence and addresses both fleets in the echo language — and the assembled crews, hearing it, respond involuntarily, the way Tamsin once did in dreams. The lie collapses publicly. Emotional beat: innocence detonating a war's pretext.

chapters.title: Justice Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Climax. With both fleets mobilizing, Tamsin hijacks the Meridian's broadcast array and transmits the full fabricated-contact record plus the children's testimony, accepting arrest by whichever side arrives first. Sefa chooses to stand with her against his own chain of command. Emotional beat: truth offered as the only remaining weapon.

chapters.title: Dreaming Again
chapters.summary: Resolution. The broadcast forces a new, honest negotiation; the architects of the lie fall, and the children become the truce's living witnesses rather than its casualties. Tamsin, awaiting a tribunal that may spare her, dreams at last in English — and in echo. Sefa sits beside her. Emotional beat: peace earned, not inherited.
